body:
The cost to paint a house interior in 2026 is $2 to $6 per square foot with a pro, which puts a 1,500 sq ft home at $3,000 to $9,000 and a 2,000 sq ft home at $4,000 to $12,000. Angi's 2026 data puts walls alone at $2.75 per square foot and walls with ceilings and trim at $4.70 per square foot. Most quotes are priced on floor area, not wall area, so check which measure a bid uses before you compare two numbers. This guide breaks the price down by home size, room, and scope, then shows a full worked example.

## Interior painting cost by home size

Floor square footage is the fastest way to budget a whole-house job. Multiply your floor area by the low and high rates to get a range, then narrow it by scope. Walls only sit near the low end. Walls, ceilings, trim, and doors together sit near the top.

| Home size (floor area) | Walls only, typical | Full scope range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1,000 sq ft | About $2,750 | $2,000 to $6,000 |
| 1,500 sq ft | About $4,125 | $3,000 to $9,000 |
| 2,000 sq ft | About $5,500 | $4,000 to $12,000 |
| 2,500 sq ft | About $6,875 | $5,000 to $15,000 |
| 3,000 sq ft | About $8,250 | $6,000 to $18,000 |

The walls-only column uses Angi's $2.75 per square foot figure, so 2,000 x $2.75 = $5,500. The full range uses the $2 to $6 band from the same 2026 data. HomeGuide prices single rooms at $300 to $1,000 each, with labor at $1 to $3 per square foot of wall or ceiling surface, which is a different measure and explains why a HomeGuide room quote can look lower than an Angi whole-house quote. Ask every painter, in writing, whether the rate is per square foot of floor or of painted surface.

Single-room prices help when you plan one room at a time. Angi lists bedrooms at $300 to $750, bathrooms at $200 to $500, kitchens at $570 to $1,210, and living rooms at $900 to $2,000. Small rooms cost more per foot because setup, masking, and cleanup take the same time in any room.

## Worked example: a 1,800 sq ft, three-bedroom home

Say you want walls and ceilings in a 1,800 sq ft home, two coats, walls in good shape, trim left for later. Here is the pro math at the walls-plus-ceilings level.

- Start with the full band: 1,800 x $2 = $3,600 low, and 1,800 x $6 = $10,800 high.
- Use the middle scope rate. Walls plus ceilings sit below the $4.70 walls, ceilings, and trim rate, so plan on about $4 per square foot.
- Typical total: 1,800 x $4 = $7,200.

Check it a second way by rooms. Three bedrooms at about $600 each is $1,800, a living room at $1,400, a kitchen at $900, two bathrooms at $350 each is $700, and halls at $800. The room-by-room sum is $1,800 + $1,400 + $900 + $700 + $800 = $5,600 for walls, plus ceilings across the home at roughly $1 to $2 per square foot of ceiling on part of the plan. That lands near the same $7,000 area, so the $7,200 budget holds up.

Now the paint itself. Say the measured wall area is 2,400 sq ft and ceilings add 1,800 sq ft, for 4,200 sq ft of surface. Two coats means 8,400 sq ft of coverage. At 350 sq ft per gallon, 8,400 / 350 = 24 gallons. Paint is sold in whole gallons, so you round up and buy 24 gallons, plus a spare for touch-ups. At $15 to $50 per gallon from HomeGuide's 2026 paint prices, the wall and ceiling paint alone runs $360 to $1,200, before primer, tape, and rollers. Our [paint calculator](/blog/paint-calculator/) does this room-by-room count for you.

## What changes the price per square foot?

Prep is the biggest swing after size. Walls with nail holes, small cracks, and glossy old paint need filling, sanding, and sometimes primer before color goes on. A home smoked in for years, or one going from dark red walls to pale gray, can need a stain-blocking primer coat and a third finish coat. Each added coat adds labor and a gallon or two.

- Ceilings over 9 ft (2.7 m) slow down cutting in and rolling, and two-story foyers need scaffold time.
- Trim, doors, and crown molding are detailed brush work, priced at $1 to $4 per linear foot for baseboards on HomeGuide.
- Kitchens and baths cost more per foot because cabinets, tile, and fixtures need careful masking.
- Empty homes paint faster. Crews charge for moving and covering furniture, or ask you to clear rooms first.
- Paint grade matters. Premium paint at the top of the $15 to $50 range covers better and often saves a third coat.

Color count adds up too. Each new color means a washed roller set, a fresh tray, and more cutting in. One color for walls and one for ceilings and trim is the cheapest plan. Our [how many coats of paint guide](/blog/how-many-coats-of-paint/) helps you judge if a quote with one coat is a real saving or a thin job.

## DIY cost vs pro cost

Doing it yourself, a single room often costs $150 to $300 in paint and supplies on HomeGuide's figures, and a whole 1,800 sq ft home lands near $500 to $1,500 if you already own ladders and brushes. Your true cost is time. A careful owner needs a full day per room for prep, two coats, and cleanup, so a whole home is several weekends.

A pro crew of two or three finishes the same home in 3 to 5 days, with sharper lines and a warranty on the work in many cases. The gap between a $1,000 DIY bill and a $7,200 pro bill is almost all labor and speed. If budget is tight, a fair split is to hire out the high ceilings, the stairwell, and the kitchen, and roll the bedrooms yourself using the [cost to paint a room guide](/blog/cost-to-paint-a-room/).

Whichever route you pick, do the unglamorous steps. Wash greasy walls near the stove, fill holes and let filler dry fully, caulk gaps at the trim, and cut in corners first, then roll while the edges are still wet. Skipping prep is the main reason fresh paint peels or flashes within a year. If old texture is coming off first, budget that as its own job before the paint quotes start.

## How to get a fair quote

Get three written quotes with the same scope list: rooms, ceilings yes or no, trim yes or no, number of coats, paint brand and grade, and who moves the furniture. A quote that just says a total price tells you nothing when the crew arrives.

Ask what prep is included in hours, not in promises. Ask if patching beyond small nail holes costs extra, and get that rate in writing. Check that doors are counted, because a home can have 15 to 20 doors and each one is real brush time. Contractors who price with a tool like our [painting estimate calculator](/blog/painting-estimate-calculator/) can usually show you the line items behind the total, which makes the bids easy to compare.

Book in late fall or winter if you can. Interior crews are busiest in spring, and off-season scheduling sometimes earns a small discount or a faster start date. Pay a deposit, pay the rest on completion, and walk every room in daylight before the final check.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to paint a 2,000 sq ft house interior?
At $2 to $6 per square foot, a pro charges $4,000 to $12,000. Walls alone at Angi's $2.75 rate come to $5,500, and walls with ceilings and trim at $4.70 come to $9,400. Good walls and one color keep you near the low half.

### How much paint do I need for a whole house interior?
Count your painted surface, double it for two coats, and divide by 350 sq ft per gallon. A home with 4,200 sq ft of walls and ceilings needs 8,400 / 350 = 24 gallons for two coats. Round up to whole gallons and keep one spare for touch-ups.

### Is it cheaper to paint one room at a time?
Per room, no. Set-up and minimum fees repeat on every visit, and HomeGuide notes some painters charge a $250 to $500 minimum per project. Whole-house jobs spread that cost out, so the per-room price drops. One room at a time still suits a tight monthly budget.

### Do painters charge extra for ceilings and trim?
Yes, most do. Angi's rate rises from $2.75 per square foot for walls alone to $4.70 with ceilings and trim added. HomeGuide lists ceiling painting at $1 to $2 per square foot and baseboard painting at $1 to $4 per linear foot.

### How long does it take to paint a whole house interior?
A pro crew usually needs 3 to 5 days for a 1,500 to 2,000 sq ft home with two coats, plus drying time between coats. One owner working alone should plan on several weekends. High ceilings, heavy prep, and many colors add days either way.

### Can I save money by buying the paint myself?
Sometimes, but ask first. Many painters get trade discounts of 20 percent or more and prefer paint they know. If you buy, agree on the exact brand and grade in writing, because cheap paint that needs a third coat costs more in labor than it saved at the store.

## Next step
Price your biggest room first with our [paint calculator](/blog/paint-calculator/), then ask two or three painters to quote the same written scope for the whole home. That one page of scope notes is what turns three vague totals into bids you can compare.

*Prices are US figures from 2026 and vary by region and supplier.*
